title: Documentation
text: Math Notes is an inline calculator that runs entirely in your browser. Type calculations line by line and each result appears beside it as dimmed ghost text, with a running total at the bottom. It is inspired by Numi and Soulver. This guide covers every feature in depth. Keep it open while you work — it is the long-form reference for the app.

title: How to read this guide
text: How to read this guide Each page focuses on one area and builds from the simple case to the edge cases. Example blocks are real calculations: use Copy to take one away, or Open in Math Notes to try it in the app in a new tab. Nothing you open replaces the sheet you already have. Everything runs locally. Your sheets are saved in your browser's storage and are never sent to a server.

title: What Math Notes is not
text: What Math Notes is not It is not a general-purpose programming environment and it is not a spreadsheet. It has one scope per sheet, no cell references by name, and no scripting. Its refusals are deliberate: rather than guess, it reports units that cannot be combined or a tag that has no lines as errors.

title: Getting started
text: Math Notes is a sheet of lines. You write one calculation per line and the answer appears to the right of it as a dimmed hint. There is no = button and no cell grid: the sheet recalculates as you type. A line can be a plain number, an expression, an assignment, a comment, or a label followed by an expression. The total bar at the bottom adds up every line that shows a number (by default; Settings can choose the average or the median). Assignments such as x = 5 show no result and are left out of totals, sum blocks, tag totals and group subtotals.

title: The screen
text: The screen The editor is the large text area. Its ghost layer shows results, tags and errors in place. The total bar sits under the editor and aggregates the sheet. Use its dropdown to switch between total , average and median . The footer holds text-size controls and the Share , Settings , Examples and Docs buttons. The tabs bar at the top holds separate sheets (see Files, sharing & data).

title: Results
text: Results Results are formatted with thousands separators and written with the unit or currency they carry. By default a result shows up to 3 decimal places . A value with more precision ends with an ellipsis, while the calculation itself keeps full precision. Change this in Settings → Decimal precision (see Settings & appearance). When a line cannot be evaluated, the error appears inline in red. Errors never stop the rest of the sheet from evaluating.

title: Editing
text: Editing Indentation — Tab indents and Shift+Tab outdents the current line (when the caret sits at its start or inside its leading whitespace) or a multi-line selection. Indentation is two spaces and does not change how a line is evaluated. Anywhere else Tab moves focus to the next control, and Esc leaves the editor for the tab bar (an open suggestion popup or find bar takes Esc first), so the keyboard is never trapped. Comment a line — click a line's number in the left gutter to comment or uncomment it. A line that already starts with ## just loses one #. Line numbers — the left gutter numbers

title: Autocomplete
text: Autocomplete As you type, a popup suggests the sheet's variables and #tags plus the built-in functions, keywords, constants and units. Press Ctrl+Space to open it on demand. Tab inserts the highlighted suggestion; ↑/↓ choose another, after which Enter inserts it too (as it does when you opened the popup with Ctrl+Space). Otherwise Enter just starts a new line, so finishing a word like grams never swaps it for kilograms. A word that is already a complete name opens no popup on its own. Esc dismisses.

title: First run
text: First run A first visit opens with a working Welcome sheet instead of an empty page — variables, labels, sum, tags, unit durations, percentages and dates. Use its Keep content / Clear content buttons to dismiss it or empty the sheet.

title: Offline
text: Offline Math Notes is an installable PWA. After the first visit a service worker keeps the app available offline; currency rates are cached so conversions keep working too. See App & platform.

title: Writing a sheet
text: A sheet is a list of lines evaluated from top to bottom. Each line can define a value, reference something above it, or simply produce a result. Variables live in one scope per sheet and are available to every line below their definition.

title: Comments and labels
text: Comments and labels Everything after a # followed by a space is a comment and is ignored. A label: before an expression names the line without being evaluated. This is handy for reminding yourself what a line means. A single # at the very start of a line also works as a comment. // also starts a comment, as in Numi and Soulver sheets. A line is one calculation: a ; between two statements is an error.

title: Tags
text: Tags With no space after the #, a word is a tag rather than a comment. Tags label lines so you can total them elsewhere. A line that is only tags shows their total, and sum/total/average/avg (optionally followed by of) does the same. Tagged value lines above the request are summed (tagged assignments such as lunch = 12 #food are not counted; write lunch: 12 #food). An operator after a request applies to its total. Tags can be used directly in calculations: #food 2, #food + #other. Requesting a tag with no tagged lines is reported as an error. A row with several tags is the full amount split eq

title: Variables
text: Variables Assign a value with = and reuse it on later lines. Variable names can contain spaces. A multi-word name must be consistent: monthly rent is one name, not monthly and rent. If an assignment fails (x = foo + 1), the name stays an error until it is assigned again, so later lines that use it show "x" has an error on line 2 instead of quietly using an older value. You can store a function with f(x) = … and call it later, either directly or under another name.

title: Objects
text: Objects An object groups named values, and a dot reaches a field.

title: References
text: References line(n) uses the result of line n. Only lines above can be referenced, and the value shows in place of the token while the caret is elsewhere (the raw line(3) reappears while you edit that line). prev refers to the most recent result above it. It skips comments and blank lines.

title: Reserved words
text: Reserved words A few names cannot be used as variables: prev (the previous result) total (the running-total aggregate) unit — opens a user-defined unit (unit widget = 3.5 kg) the unconditional date words today, now, yesterday, tomorrow, christmas, halloween any name starting with (the editor's internal helpers) end closes a group Variables otherwise share one scope with the built-in names, so a variable can shadow a unit or function: after m = 5, 2 m is 2 × m, not two metres. The other aggregate keywords sum, average and avg can still be shadowed: after avg = 5, a later avg line reads the vari

title: Blank lines
text: Blank lines A blank line ends the block that sum, average and the other aggregates look at, and it separates sections of a sheet. Use it to keep aggregates scoped to the lines you mean.

title: Numbers & operators
text: Math Notes evaluates expressions with the usual arithmetic operators, plus a set of word operators, number scales and rounding phrases that read like English.

title: Operators
text: Operators Operator Meaning --- --- + Add - Subtract Multiply / Divide ^ Power % Remainder ! Factorial ( ) Group Many more functions and operators are available — see the mathjs documentation. The reference lists the function aliases Math Notes adds.

title: Word operators
text: Word operators Calculations can use words instead of symbols: with and without combine and subtract durations:

title: Number scales
text: Number scales A repeated k multiplies by a thousand: 2k is 2,000, 1kk is 1,000,000, 1kkk is 1,000,000,000.

title: Percentages
text: Percentages Use of, on and off with %. A percentage can be added to or taken from a value and chained with more terms, and it can be negative.

title: Rounding
text: Rounding Round a result with a phrase at the end of the line, or call round, ceil or floor directly. Rounding works with units and currencies too. A step can carry its own unit, and a duration written in several units is rounded in the smallest one. Units and currencies round to a fraction too.

title: Number bases
text: Number bases Convert a whole number with in, to or as: 255 in hex is 0xff, 255 to bin is 0b11111111, 255 as octal is 0o377, 0x9F31 to decimal is 40,753 and 5300 in sci is 5.3e+3. The bit operators <<, , &, , ^ and ~ are exact for whole numbers well past 32 bits.

title: Constants and functions
text: Constants and functions pi and π are available, along with the standard mathjs functions and these aliases: Alias Meaning --- --- ln Natural logarithm fact Factorial arcsin, arccos, arctan Inverse trigonometric functions root(n, x) The x-th root of n See Lists & sequences for sum, mean and the other aggregate functions, and Reference for the full table.

title: Lists & sequences
text: Lists hold several values. Write one with square brackets, index it, slice it, and use mathjs functions to aggregate or transform it. Lists and ranges are capped at 100 items so a runaway sequence cannot freeze the editor. The cap covers everything that builds a list or matrix (ones, zeros, identity, random, concat, kron, …) and assigning past the end of a list (n[500] = 1).

title: Lists
text: Lists Lists are 1-indexed : n[1] is the first element. Slice with a range: Assign an element: and - work element by element, and lists combine with the mathjs functions. The plain , / and ^ follow matrix rules, so use . , ./ and .^ to multiply, divide or raise element by element: Matrices are lists of lists, indexed with two subscripts:

title: Sequences
text: Sequences A range start:end makes a list of numbers, with an optional :step. A range can be named and indexed like any other list:

title: Iteration
text: Iteration A function receives the whole list or range it is called with. A body such as x 2 or x + 1 happens to work on every element, but x x is a dot product (so sq(1:3) is 14). To apply a function to each element, use map.

title: Aggregates
text: Aggregates sum, mean, min, max and the rest of the mathjs aggregate functions accept a list or a range. sum, total, average and avg also work as bare keywords on the lines above — see Groups & totals.

title: Groups & totals
text: Math Notes aggregates in three related ways: the running total in the bottom bar, the aggregate keywords (sum, average, …) you write on a line, and named groups that show a subtotal in place.

title: The total bar
text: The total bar The total bar under the editor aggregates every numeric result in the sheet. Its dropdown switches between total (sum), average and median . Plain numbers fold into a single unit; a bare number is read in the first unit used for its dimension, so adding a larger unit later (1 day after some hours) adds to the total instead of reinterpreting the earlier numbers. Compatible units (such as cm and m) merge into the largest present for display; mixed dimensions fall back to the plain numeric sum, while mixing two currencies is an error — convert to one first.

title: Aggregate keywords
text: Aggregate keywords sum, total, average and avg aggregate the lines above, up to a blank line. A blank line starts a new block, so you can keep several independent aggregates in one sheet. The keywords can also take a tag: sum #food, or the shorthand #food on its own line (see Tags).

title: Groups
text: Groups Open a named group with a label on its own line (like Groceries:) and close it with end. The header shows the group's subtotal and the whole block is shaded. The inner lines still count in the bottom total. Groups work with units too, following the total's unit rule: Blank lines inside a group are ignored, and sum/average inside a group total that group rather than the whole sheet.

title: Interaction with prev and tags
text: Interaction with prev and tags A closed group leaves prev at the subtotal shown on its header, then continues from the end line. Tags still work across groups: a tagged row contributes its share to the tag no matter which group it sits in.

title: Mistakes
text: Mistakes A header with no end is just a label, and the lines after it are ordinary lines. An end with no open header is reported as an error. Groups do not nest: a second header inside an open group starts a new label.

title: Units & measures
text: Convert between units with to, in or as, name what you are measuring to convert across dimensions, and write rates naturally.

title: Unit conversion
text: Unit conversion A length, mass or volume written in two units is their sum, in the smaller unit, and min and sec are the minute and the second wherever a unit goes. CSS units are supported too, so you can check a layout: Areas and volumes can be written in words: 20 sq cm, 30 square inches, 5 m squared, 3 ft cubed, 11 sqm, 11 cbm or with ² and ³ (10 m²). They read as cm^2, inches^2, m^2, and so on.

title: Measurement system
text: Measurement system Cooking volume units follow the measurement system in Settings → Measurement system — Metric (default), US customary or Imperial. It sets cup to 250, 236.6 or 284.1 ml respectively, along with tsp, tbsp, fl oz, pint, quart and gallon.

title: Cooking & measures
text: Cooking & measures Convert between dimensions by naming what you are measuring. The subject is free-form and optional: a known ingredient uses its density, a fuel its energy density, media their bitrate, and anything else a default (water). Write it before to/in.

title: Rates
text: Rates A rate is one unit per another. mathjs does the arithmetic; these phrases make rates easy to write. per, a, an, at and for are all understood. The verb is optional.

title: Custom units
text: Custom units Define your own unit with unit <name = <amount . It then behaves like a built-in one: the plural works, it converts to the units it was defined from, and it merges with them. Change the definition and every use follows. The plural of the last word is generated in the usual English ways (box/boxes, bus/buses, leaf/leaves, potato/potatoes) and ão becomes ões or ães; for any other plural, use the singular. A name may contain several words or accents, and a unit can be built from another. Definitions are scoped to the sheet that contains them, so removing the line removes the unit. un

title: The unit rule
text: The unit rule Units only combine in shapes that mean something. kg L, BRL hour, h^2 and m^0.5 are reported as errors rather than as strange combined units. Money only forms ratios (USD/hour, USD/km), so use a rate when you want to convert a currency across time or distance.

title: Money & currencies
text: Convert between currencies using 3-letter ISO codes or symbols. Rates come from the European Central Bank via Frankfurter and are cached locally so conversions keep working offline. While a window stays open the rates are re-checked every hour; if a check fails or takes longer than 10 seconds, the cached rates are used and a short notice says so.

title: Converting
text: Converting

title: How results are written
text: How results are written Results use the currency's symbol where it has one (350usd becomes US$ 350); currencies without a symbol keep their ISO code. A rate reads as a phrase: 100 USD/hour becomes US$ 100 per hour.

title: Money only forms ratios
text: Money only forms ratios A currency can be divided by another unit to make a rate (USD/hour, USD/km, USD/kg), but it cannot be multiplied by an unrelated unit. BRL hour is reported as an error rather than as a strange combined unit — use a rate instead. A symbol and a code together ($30 CAD, €5 EUR) mean the code's currency.

title: Supported codes
text: Supported codes AUD, BRL, CAD, CHF, CNY, CZK, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, HUF, IDR, ILS, INR, ISK, JPY, KRW, MXN, MYR, NOK, NZD, PHP, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, THB, TRY, USD, ZAR. A currency symbol such as $, €, £ or R$ works wherever a code does, including as the target of a conversion ($5 to €, 5 EUR in R$). Autocomplete completes a code from its first letters.

title: Dates & time
text: Math Notes understands calendar dates, clock times and durations. Dates can be written in several styles, stored in variables, and combined with time units.

title: Writing dates
text: Writing dates A date can be written as 10 June, June 10, 2023, 2019-04-01 or 12/02/1988. A date with numbers only is read day first (12/02/1988 is 12 February; 02/13/2024 is not a date), so write 2019-04-01 when it must not be ambiguous. Yearless dates resolve to their nearest occurrence, and a date can be saved in a variable: The unconditional date words today, now, yesterday, tomorrow, christmas and halloween are always available.

title: Calendar arithmetic
text: Calendar arithmetic Add or subtract time units from a date, or phrase it with after/before.

title: Intervals
text: Intervals Subtracting one date from another gives the interval between them. through … in days, midpoint between … and … and days since/between are also understood. An explicit year keeps the whole interval, so 2019-01-10 - 2020-02-05 does not wrap.

title: Date parts
text: Date parts Ask for a single part of a date with a phrase:

title: Workdays & work hours
text: Workdays & work hours Workdays are Monday to Friday, and a full work day is eight hours. Public holidays are not counted yet.

title: Formatting a date
text: Formatting a date Use as with a pattern to format a date.

title: Clock times
text: Clock times A clock time such as 9:45 am, 1:30 or 16:00 takes durations and measures intervals. Clock times show in 24-hour by default; Settings → Clock switches to 12-hour.

title: Timespans
text: Timespans Show a duration as a timespan of components, or split it into two units. A timespan is a real duration, so it can be added and multiplied, and converted to a single unit with to/in/as. Because a timespan is a real value, it can be referenced like any other:

title: Files, sharing & data
text: Math Notes keeps your work on your device. There is no account and no server: sheets are saved in your browser, backed up in a versioned local store, and shared only when you choose to.

title: Tabs
text: Tabs Use the tabs at the top to keep separate worksheets. Every tab is saved automatically as you type. Switch — click a tab (or use ←/→ once focused, or Ctrl+Tab). Reorder — click and drag a tab to a new position. Rename — double-click the tab name (or press F2 on a focused tab; on a touchscreen, press and hold). Close — click the ×, or press Delete / Backspace on a focused tab (you are asked to confirm). Closing the last tab opens a fresh one. Add — click the + tab, or the ⌄ beside it to start from a template (budget, trip cost, invoice, savings goal, split a bill).

title: Export and import
text: Export and import Use Settings → Files to download the active sheet as a text file, or load one from a file (.txt, .numi or plain text, up to 1 MB). Importing replaces the content of the active sheet , after asking for confirmation if the sheet is not empty; it does not open a new tab. Exports are named math-notes-YYYY-MM-DD.txt. The same actions are on ⇧⌘E / Ctrl+Shift+E (export) and ⇧⌘I / Ctrl+Shift+I (import). A .numi file is read as plain text, so only what Math Notes understands carries over. Comments start with # or //; quoted text next to a value is an error; and/xor are not word operat

title: Share links
text: Share links The Share button copies a link that carries the active sheet inside it. Anyone who opens it is asked whether to open the sheet in a new tab; it never replaces what they already have. The link is compressed, and you are warned if it grows past about 8,000 characters, since some apps cut long links; a link that unpacks to more than 256 KB is refused. Nothing is uploaded. The sheet travels in the link's # fragment, which browsers never send to a server — it does not land in an access log and is not forwarded in a Referer header.

title: Auto-saved snapshots
text: Auto-saved snapshots Every tab's edits are backed up to IndexedDB as versioned snapshots. Open Settings → Recover to see every snapshot, grouped by tab, and restore any of them, or use Restore all from latest backup to bring back every tab. It puts each tab's latest snapshot back and leaves tabs without one, their order and the active tab alone. Sheets the app fills in for you (a template, a shared sheet, Welcome) are backed up as soon as they open. Each tab keeps its 10 most recent snapshots, saved a couple of seconds after you stop typing. Closing a tab also removes its snapshots. Snapshots

title: Reset
text: Reset Settings → Reset → Reset data clears the theme, tabs and all stored data back to their defaults, then opens a fresh Welcome sheet and restarts the tab counter. Export anything you want to keep first.

title: Privacy
text: Privacy Sheets stay on your device. The only network request the app makes is for currency rates, and those are cached for offline use. See About for the libraries involved.

title: Settings & appearance
text: Open Settings from the footer. Choices are remembered in your browser and applied the next time you open the app.

title: Theme
text: Theme Choose a light or dark theme. The palette is applied through CSS variables, so every surface of the app changes together. There are five themes: One Dark (the default), Dracula , Solarized Dark , Monokai and Light .

title: Text size
text: Text size The footer's − / + step the editor text between 50% and 200% of your browser's default font size, with Reset size back to 100%. Because it scales from your browser's size, it respects the text size you have already chosen for accessibility.

title: Decimal precision
text: Decimal precision Results show up to 3 decimal places by default. Set the number of places from 0 to 10 in Settings → Decimal precision . A truncated result ends with an ellipsis (…); the calculation itself keeps full precision, so later lines that use the result are not affected by the display choice.

title: Clock
text: Clock Clock times use a 24-hour format by default. Settings → Clock switches to a 12-hour format with am/pm.

title: Measurement system
text: Measurement system Cooking volume units follow Settings → Measurement system — Metric (default), US customary or Imperial . It sets cup to 250, 236.6 or 284.1 ml, and changes tsp, tbsp, fl oz, pint, quart and gallon with it. See Units & measures.

title: Language
text: Language The interface, the Examples and these documentation pages ship in English , Portuguese and Spanish . Math Notes starts in your system language and can be changed in Settings → Language . The calculator syntax itself stays English regardless of the interface language.

title: Files, recovery and reset
text: Files, recovery and reset The Settings dialog also holds Files (export and import), Recover (restore from automatic snapshots) and Reset . They are described in Files, sharing & data.

title: App & platform
text: Math Notes is a progressive web app: it installs like a native app, works offline, and respects your system preferences.

title: Install
text: Install Open the app in a modern browser and use the browser's Install or Add to Home Screen action. Once installed it launches in its own window, with no address bar or browser chrome.

title: Offline
text: Offline A service worker keeps the app available offline. After the first visit, the app shell and its code are served from the cache; a new version is installed in the background and takes over on a later visit, once every tab has closed, so an open page never mixes versions. Currency rates are cached too, so conversions keep working offline using the most recent rates the app has seen.

title: Accessibility
text: Accessibility The text size control scales from your browser's default size, so it honours your system preference. The editor has an accessible label, the status bar announces state with aria-live, and the active line's result is announced through a separate polite live region. The autocomplete keeps the editor a plain text box (aria-controls, aria-autocomplete) and announces the number of suggestions and the highlighted one through a status message. Tabs can be renamed from the keyboard (F2) or by touch (press and hold). The tab bar is a roving-tabindex tablist: Tab reaches it in one stop, ←/

title: Reserved words
text: Reserved words prev, total, unit, today, now, yesterday, tomorrow, christmas, halloween, end, and any name starting with cannot be used as variable names. unit opens a custom unit.

title: About
text: Math Notes is a browser-based inline calculator, inspired by Numi and Soulver. Its source is open — see the GitHub repository. Calculations run on mathjs, an extensible math library for JavaScript. Currency conversion rates come from the European Central Bank via Frankfurter.

title: Privacy
text: Privacy Your sheets stay on your device. They are saved in your browser's storage and are never sent to a server. Share links carry the sheet in the URL fragment, which browsers do not transmit with the request. See Files, sharing & data.

title: Interface languages
text: Interface languages The interface, the Examples and these documentation pages are available in English, Portuguese and Spanish. The calculator syntax is always English. Switch the app's language in Settings → Language .

title: Credits
text: Credits Math Notes is open source. The documentation is generated from Markdown at build time and published as static pages alongside the app.
